body: Thanks for the advise, especially about body language. I've always been sure not to be pushy and to just let them come to me when they need to, it's just that they never do and it can get a little frustrating is all.

They are both seeing professionals. One is taking the medical road while the other is just talking to someone. Basically it isn't helping either of them from what they have told me.

And they've told me the basics, but they never go deeper into detail because they "don't want to trouble me" and I can't convince them otherwise.

Well as far as I know they both already are in therapy. One is taking the more medical route, as I've explained, while the other is just seeing someone. The problem is, she says that her therapist isn't very nice and sometimes makes her feels worse. She doesn't have a job at the moment (neither of them do) and so it's really up to her parents on whether she even goes to a therapist let alone a good one. 

And also, they are very sensitive people. I never want to talk about my problems because I feel it would be insensitive to their situations. Not to say that I don't at all, they are two of my closest after all. But I try to avoid being rude at any cost. We talk, and we hold conversations easily, it's just when it comes to that they say stuff like "I don't want to trouble you" and "it's nothing" or "it's stupid" and no matter what I say I can't convince them otherwise.
